requirements.text: If there are more than three ongoing incidents, do not proceed with retirement and instead update the service status to non-operational
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_017' AND status = 'non-operational'
assumptions: the SAP ERP service is SVC_017 (name 'SAP ERP', status operational on the seed); SVC_018 'SAP QA' is the near match, covered by a stay

active / ongoing means status not in (resolved, closed) under the policy 3.3 lifecycle; SVC_017 has four such incidents on the seed (INC_001 in_progress; INC_044, INC_069, INC_082 on_hold; INC_052 resolved is excluded), so 4 > 3 takes the non-operational branch
'non-operational' is a seed value of service.status (6 rows); the policy lists no service enumeration
the check on the incidents is a read and leaves no state, so no incident row changes

requirements.text: ensure all related service offerings are updated to reflect the same status
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_021' AND status = 'non-operational'
assumptions: SVCOFF_021 ('SAP ERP - Financials') is one of the three offerings with business_service = 'SVC_017' on the seed (SVCOFF_021, SVCOFF_022, SVCOFF_038), all operational
'the same status' is the service's new status, non-operational (the seed's spelling, with a hyphen)

disagreement: business_service: A adds business_service = 'SVC_017' to the sql, B does not; chose to leave it out because the anchor already names the row and the request does not change an offering's parent service, so the predicate would test an unrequested invariant

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_017' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: what the request forbids: with four ongoing incidents the service must not be retired; 'retired' is a seed value of service.status (6 rows)
overlaps the non-operational change, which also fails if the service is retired; it is the forbidden action named on its own

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_018' AND status = 'repair_in_progress'
assumptions: boundary of 'the SAP ERP service': SVC_018 'SAP QA' (description 'ERP Quality Assurance') is the other SAP service on the seed, the row a loose reading would sweep in; it keeps its seed status

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_023' AND status = 'repair_in_progress'
assumptions: boundary of 'related service offerings': SVCOFF_023 'SAP QA - Refresh' is the only other SAP offering on the seed (business_service SVC_018, not SVC_017) and keeps its status

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that SVC_017 is not retired (status = 'retired', expected 0); B has it, A does not, reading the non-operational change as already excluding retirement; kept because 'do not proceed with retirement' is an action the request forbids in its own words, and the stay names that action even though the non-operational change also fails if it is taken; its cell holds the counted value retired, matching its sql.
disagreement: value: business_service in the offering requirements: A's sql for SVCOFF_021, SVCOFF_022 and SVCOFF_038 adds business_service = 'SVC_017', and for the SVCOFF_023 stay business_service = 'SVC_018', B's does not; chose to leave it out because each row is anchored by id and the request does not change an offering's parent service, so the predicate would test an unrequested invariant; the parent service is stated in the assumptions.
The branch depends on how 'active' / 'ongoing' is read: counting new, in_progress and on_hold gives four incidents on SVC_017 and the non-operational branch the benchmark's checks expect; counting only in_progress would give one and no change, which the benchmark does not expect, so the wider reading is taken.
The benchmark's queries use double-quoted string literals, which SQLite reads as strings here; the requirements use single quotes.
